title: Salary Equity and DEI Analysis
text:
In this project, we analyze an employee dataset to answer a critical question in organizations: Is there a gender pay gap unexplained by factors such as experience, education, or department? In other words, we are looking to identify whether there is a gap unexplained by the factors that commonly influence salary levels in a company. As HR Professionals, I am sure my company measures people’s capabilities by their hard and soft skills, and not by their gender? We would all love to live in this perfect world. But the reality is that biases exist, and discovering and limiting them is our job.
More than a simple analysis of the provided data, I seek to build a model that allows us to isolate the effect of gender on salary, controlling for other truly relevant variables. I invite you to reflect: It is already difficult enough to be a woman in Mexico, without being questioned simply because of how you were born.

By deeply understanding the quality of the dataset or the data we’re working with, we can perform better analysis, use more efficient methods, and choose algorithms that make sense.
If our data isn’t properly prepared, the insights won’t be reliable. There will be unexplained errors and biases, or simply everything will be wrong. It’s crucial to have good judgment and know how to handle cleaning and preparation, so we can make the best use of the data we have available. Summary of Changes
The following transformations were performed on the DataFrame:
1. Text Standardization: - Categorical (text) columns: Department, Gender, Status, Location. Were cleaned by removing extra spaces and standardizing the uppercase/lowercase format. To avoid comparison errors between “HR” and “hr” or ” HR “.
2. Imputation of Missing Values: - Numeric variables (Performance Score or Age): null values were replaced with the median of each column. This is a best practice in data analysis that minimizes the impact of outliers. And maintains high dataset integrity, instead of deleting all records that have missing values. - Categorical variables: a label called “Not Specified” was created to still keep records of incomplete data and not shrink the dataset.
Creation of New Variables: -Tenure_Years: The years elapsed since the joining date are calculated. Up to the current date. This variable adds more interpretive capacity, to analyze how experience in the company impacts salary. -Performance_Cat: We took the Performance Score which had a value from 1-5 and converted it into a categorical variable assigning values such as (Low, Medium, High). This way it is easier to perform a comparative analysis by performance levels.
CHECKPOINT we now have a dataset without inconsistencies or null values. We are ready to perform an exploratory analysis and a statistical model.

Figure 1: Figura 4.1: Distribución de salario por género (boxplot)





Análisis: Este boxplot muestra la distribución completa del salario para cada género. La línea central representa la mediana, la caja el rango intercuartílico, y los puntos fuera de la caja son valores atípicos. Esto nos permite identificar visualmente si existen diferencias en la dispersión y tendencia central entre géneros. Podemos observar una distribución equilibrada de géneros. Existe una diferencia de 5.14% a favor de los hombres. Sin embargo, usando Prueba T el p-value es 0.0934 con un alfa de .05, esto significa que no podemos que existe una brecha salarial sistemática por género. Debemos analizar otras variables que tengan mayor efecto en la brecha salarial.








Figure 2: Figura 4.2: Salario por Departamento y Genero





Analysis: Comparison of average salary broken down by department and gender. This visualization allows us to identify in which areas the salary differences between genders are more pronounced, and which departments have higher or lower compensation overall.
Here we observe that there is indeed a gap in the HR and Sales departments in favor of men. However, in the IT department, women have the advantage in the salary gap. Here we can begin to observe that the Department has more influence on the salary gap than gender. Or at least it can explain it a little better.








Figure 3: Figura 4.3: Salary vs Tenure





Analysis: Trend of average salary as years of experience increase. This graph reveals how compensation evolves throughout a career and whether salary growth is linear, exponential, or stagnates at certain points.
This graph shows us something very interesting. Experience does not predict salary in this company using this data. There is no correlation between Experience and Salary. The problem this company has likely has one of its roots here, as the progression system has many flaws or does not exist.








Figure 4: Figura 4.4: Relationship between Salary and Performance





Analysis: Average salary by performance category, with error bars showing variability (standard deviation). This allows us to evaluate whether there is a clear correlation between high performance and higher compensation, and how consistent this relationship is within each category. Upon conducting an ANOVA test, we observe that performance does not have a significant impact on salary. Employees with a Score of 1 (low performance) earn higher salaries than those with a Score of 5 (high performance). While we cannot draw definitive conclusions at this stage, an initial diagnosis suggests that the problem may stem from a poorly designed incentive system.

6. Business Conclusions and Recommendations

Executive Summary
The analysis performed on our dataset reveals two key findings. First, there is no gender-based salary gap in this case. While this might be somewhat surprising, we can be confident that if the opposite were true, our robust analysis would have identified it. The second conclusion is that the compensation system is highly unusual (due to the synthetic nature of the dataset), and we observe no relationship between performance or experience and salary grade. In other words, in this analysis, employee performance and tenure do not serve to predict salary.


KEY INSIGHTS - Hard Data

The insights presented help us think about how a dataset with this behavior impacts talent and the organization. We can answer problems that haven’t arrived yet, anticipate them. We have two insights that speak to talent. The current compensation system is not working because employees have no incentive to stay with the company. There is no clear path to earn more, and while this may not be the only reason people work, it is one of the main drivers. It is also important to highlight that employees categorized as high performers are at risk of turnover. This is where companies can lose a lot of money and key know-how that they don’t have in monetary terms, but which greatly impacts processes, organizational culture, and collective sentiment.


RECOMMENDATIONS
Short Term (0-3 months): - A complete audit of the current compensation system is needed, identifying which KPIs are driving raises and aligning everything more closely with performance.
Medium Term (3-12 months): - Redesign of internal salary grades. Establish a more robust salary scale that includes variables aligned with performance, business impact, tenure, career development, and key positions. Promote the design of a system based on clear expectations and measurable objectives.
Long Term (12+ months): - Work with Executive Leadership, Human Resources, and Compensation teams to implement a more transparent system aligned with business objectives and strategy.


LIMITATIONS
The most important thing to highlight is that this dataset has very atypical patterns. But IF THIS CAN BE SEEN IN THE EXAMPLE, IT CAN BE REPLICATED IN REAL LIFE WITH REAL DATA!


NEXT STEPS
To deepen the analysis, the following is recommended: - Integrate turnover data. Provide precise follow-up to employees who have the best performance. This signals to other employees that their performance is very important for retention and building their own career. - It would be very interesting to observe the relationship between new variables such as education and certifications, to analyze how they impact salary, performance, and whether they explain more of a salary gap.

Más que un análisis simple de los datos proporcionados. Busco construir un modelo que nos permita aislar el efecto del género sobre el salario, controlando por otras variables realmente relevantes. Antes de hacer cualquier análisis, necesitamos hacer una limpieza del dataset y preparar los datos. Este paso es probablemnte el mas importante. Al entender a profundidad la calidad del dataset o de los datos con los cuales trabajamos, podemos realizar un mejor análisis, usar métodos más eficientes, elegir algoritmos que hagan sentido. Si no tenemos nuestros datos preparados, los insights no serán confiables. Habrá errores y sesgos inexplicables, o simplemente todod estará mal. Es crucial tener criterio y saber como manejar la limpieza y preparación, para poder hacer el mejor uso de los datos que si tenemos disponibles. No se pueden hacer milagros, pero si se pueden reducir los errores.


Code
# 1. Limpieza de texto en columnas categóricas (ejemplo: 'Department' o 'Job Title')

Resumen de Cambios
Se realizaron las siguientes transformaciones en el DataFrame:
1. Estandarizacion del texto: - Las columnas categóricas (texto) : Deparment, Gender, Status, Location. Fueron limpiadas eliminando espacios extra y estandarizando el formato de mayscula/minuscula. Para evitar errores de comparación entre ¨HR¨ y ¨hr¨ o ¨ HR ¨.
2. Imputación de valores faltantes (missing values): - Variables numéricas (Performance Score o Age): los valores nulos se reemplazaron con la mediana de cada columna. Esta es una mejor práctica en el análisis de datos que minimiza el impacto por valores atípicos. Y mantiene una alta integridad del dataset, en lugar de borrar todos los records que tienen valores faltantes. -Variables categóricas: se creo una etiqueda llamada ¨No Especificado¨ para aun así mantener registros de datos incompletos y no achicar el dataset.
Creación de Nuevas variables: -Antiguedad_Años : Se calculan los años transcurridos desde la fecha de ingreso. Hasta la fecha actual. Esta variable añade mas capacidad de interpretación, para analizar como la experiencia en la empresa impacta el salario. -Performance_Cat: Tomamos el Performance Score que tenia un valor del 1-5 y lo convertimos en una variable categorica asignando valores como (Bajo, Medio, Alto). De esta forma es mas facil realizar un análisis comparativo por niveles de rendimiento.
CHECKPOINT ahora tenenemos un dataset sin inconsistencias, ni valores nulos. Estamos listos para realizar un análisis exploratorio y un modelo estadístico.

text:
6. Conclusiones y Recomendaciones de Negocio

Resumen Ejecutivo
El análisis realizado sobre el dataset que trabajamos, nos arroja un par de cosas. Primero, es que en este caso no hay brecha salarial que sea explicada por genero. Aunque esto puede ser un poco deconcertante, podemos estar tranquilos de que si fuese lo contrario, nuestro robusto análisis lo podría identificar. La segunda conclusion es que el sistema de compensación es muuuy raro (por la naturaleza sintética del dataset), y observamos que no hay relación entre performance o experiencia y el grado salarial. Es decir, en este análisis el desempeño y la antiguedad de los empleados, no nos sirven para predecir el salario.


INSIGHTS CLAVE - Datos Duros
Brecha de género no significativa | Diferencia de 5.14%, p=0.0934, Cohen’s d=0.13 | No hay evidencia de discriminación salarial sistemática. | | Experiencia no predice salario | r=0.004, p=0.985 | El sistema actual de progresión salarial no está funcionando. | | Performance no impacta salario | r=0.002, p=0.879 | Riesgo alto de fuga de talento de alto rendimiento. | | Modelo predictivo débil | R²=0.004, F-test p=0.662 | Factores no observados dominan la compensación. |
Los insights presentados nos ayudan a pensar en como un dataset con este comportamiento impacta en el talento y en la organizacion. Podemos darle respuesta a problemas que aun no llegan, anticiparnos. Tenemos dos insights que nos hablan del talento. El sistema de compensación actual no esta funcionando, porque los empleados no tienen un incentivo para permanecer en la empresa. No hay un camino claro a ganas mas y aunque este no sea la única razón por la cual la gente trabaja, es uno de los principales drivers. También es importante destacar que los empleados catalogados con un Desmepeño alto, estan en riesgo de rotación. Aqui se puede perder muchísimo dinero y know-how clave que las empresas no tienen en terminos monetarios, pero que impactan muchísimo los procesos, la cultura organizacional y el sentimiento colectivo.


RECOMENDACIONES
Corto Plazo (0-3 meses): -(Se necesita una auditoría completa del actual sistema de compensaciónes, cuales son los KPIs que estan decidiendo los aumentos y alinear más todo al desempeño)
Mediano Plazo (3-12 meses): -(Rediseño de grados salariales intra-empresa. Establecer un tabulador mas robusto que contenga variables alineadas con el desempeño, impacto de negocio, antiguedad, carrera, y posiciones clave. Impulsando el diseño de un sistema basado en expectativas claras y objetivos medibles).
Largo Plazo (12+ meses): -(Trabajar con Dirección, Recursos Humanos y Compensaciones, para implementar un sistema mas transparente y alineado a los objetivos y estrategia de negocio).


LIMITACIONES
Lo más importante a destacar es que este dataset tiene patrones muy atípicos. Pero SI SE PUEDE VER ESTO EN EL EJEMPLO, SE PUEDE REPLICAR EN LA VIDA REAL CON DATOS REALES!


SIGUIETES PASOS
Para profundizar en el análisis se recomienda lo siguiente: -Integrar datos de rotación. Darle seguimiento puntual a los empleados que tienen el mejor desmpeño. Esto da una señal a los demas empleados que su desempeño es muy importante para retención y construcción de su propia carrera. -Sería muy interesante observar la relación entre nuevas variables como educación y certificaciónes, para analizar como impacta en salario, desempeño y si explica mas una brecha salarial.

title: People Analytics Tech Stack: From Reactive to Proactive
text:
This is a mock challenge prepared in advance for an interview at Sofia. The starting point of our journey is the Voice of the Customer(Employees) process in place. Currently the manual labor takes about 15 hours per week. This contributes to a reactionary culture, instead of anticipating the needs of our high-performers to enable more importante and valuable work.     emp['location'] = random.choice(locations)

    emp['hire_date'] = (datetime(2026, 6, 23) - timedelta(days=days_ago)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    emp['tenure_years'] = round(days_ago / 365.25, 1)
    
    if days_ago >= 180 and random.random() < 0.6:
        promo_days_ago = random.randint(30, days_ago - 30)
        emp['last_promotion_date'] = (datetime(2026, 6, 23) - timedelta(days=promo_days_ago)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')

    else:

    base_salaries = {

        'Lead': (100000, 160000), 'Manager': (130000, 200000), 'Director': (180000, 300000)
    }

    emp['bonus_pct'] = round(np.random.uniform(0, 20), 1)
    midpoint = (min_sal + max_sal) / 2
    emp['compa_ratio'] = round(emp['base_salary'] / midpoint, 2)
    
    emp['performance_score'] = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], p=[0.05, 0.15, 0.50, 0.25, 0.05])
    emp['last_review_date'] = (datetime(2026, 6, 23) - timedelta(days=random.randint(30, 365))).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    
    emp['engagement_score'] = round(np.random.uniform(1, 10), 1)
    emp['satisfaction_score'] = round(np.random.uniform(1, 10), 1)
    
    if random.random() < TURNOVER_RATE:
        emp['status'] = 'Left'
        left_days_ago = random.randint(30, min(days_ago, 730))
        emp['termination_date'] = (datetime(2026, 6, 23) - timedelta(days=left_days_ago)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        emp['termination_type'] = np.random.choice(termination_types, p=[0.70, 0.15, 0.15])

            emp['satisfaction_score'] = round(np.clip(np.random.normal(4, 1.5), 1, 6), 1)
            emp['compa_ratio'] = round(np.clip(np.random.normal(0.85, 0.1), 0.6, 1.0), 2)

        "Estoy considerando otras opciones porque siento que no avanzo aquí.",

def generate_survey(status, engagement):
    if status == 'Left' or engagement < 4:
        theme = 'negative'
    elif engagement > 7:
        theme = 'positive'
    else:
        theme = 'neutral'
    
    base_response = random.choice(survey_themes[theme])

    return base_response
